sources.title: Palorchestes azael, candidate for Victoria fossil emblem
sources.author: Ursula Smith, Museums Victoria; photograph Benjamin Healley
sources.evidence: Actual P216490 skull/mandibles image inspected. No complete skeleton; buffalo size. Current reconstruction favors prehensile lip rather than trunk, since trunk muscle attachment evidence absent.
sources.rights: Skull photo CC BY4.0 Museums Victoria / Benjamin Healley; private reference.

sources.title: The extraordinary osteology and functional morphology of the limbs in Palorchestidae
sources.author: Richards, Wells, Evans, Fitzgerald and Adams (2019)
sources.evidence: Fig3 actual humeri NMVP159792 and NHMUKPVOR46914; Fig9 unassociated unguals NMVP252196/P159792, both with50mm bars inspected. Deep thin recurved claws, not retractile. Body mass estimates and uncertain partial manus explicitly discussed.
sources.rights: CC BY4.0 authors, private reference photos not texture assets.

sources.title: Low elbow mobility indicates unique forelimb posture and function in a giant extinct marsupial
sources.author: Richards, Bishop, Hocking, Adams and Evans (2021)
sources.evidence: Quantitative ROM indicates strongly crouched abducted forelimbs, not completely fused elbow; contrasted with more columnar Zygomaturus. Wholebody posture remains inference, no attributable trackway.
